title: Turing Morphogenesis & Reaction-Diffusion Typography
discipline: Morphogenetic Chemistry · Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations · Gray-Scott Model · Reaction-Diffusion
hypothesis: Can digital typography be formulated as an active reaction-diffusion substrate governed by Alan Turing's 1952 non-linear partial differential equations, where letterforms seeded in a Gray-Scott chemical matrix balance activator-inhibitor kinetics to organically morph between stable structural glyphs, mitotic dividing letterforms, and self-organizing labyrinthine ribbons across Pearson parameter space (F, k), demonstrating that biological morphogenesis can replace static Bézier geometry with living organic form?
